subject: Post-demo performance recap & decision checklist
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Aria Gupta <aria.gupta@medicore.com>, Liam Carter <liam.carter@medicore.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo performance recap & decision checklist

Hi Aria / Liam —

Thanks again for taking the time today to walk through the live demo. Quick written recap so we’re all aligned on what we observed versus the decision criteria you described. I’ve attached the raw benchmark CSV and a short checklist for your review.

What we ran during the demo (short):
- Model: open-llama-20b-quant (single-stream, FP16 kernels where supported)
- Typical prompt: 120 tokens in, ~60 tokens out (prioritized streaming)
- Observed: p50 request latency ~58ms, p95 request latency ~235ms (single-host, isolated test harness), sustained throughput ~110 reqs/min at 100 concurrent connections, streaming token latency ~40–60ms per token under demo conditions.

We captured these as baseline numbers in 20260502-demo-benchmarks.csv. These are synthetic but representative of the workload you described. Important caveats: demo used short sequences and warm KV cache; real user mix may widen p95.

Decision criteria you asked us to confirm (please annotate if I’ve misunderstood):
1) End-user perceived latency: p95 <= 250ms for single-turn queries (non-streaming ok as a fallback).
2) Streaming responsiveness: initial token within 100ms, subsequent tokens <= 75ms token-latency.
3) Concurrency & throughput: sustain 100 concurrent requests with burst to 250 for short periods (~2–3 minutes).
4) Operational: 99.9% availability for production windows, and quantized variants available to reduce unit cost.

Requested next steps (my recommended MAP items):
- Connor (me): Deliver the raw benchmark CSV + concise SLO checklist (attached) and a one-page explanation of trade-offs between dedicated vs hosted.
- Diego (SE): Schedule a deep technical perf call to validate the real request mix and load profile — propose Tue/Wed next week.
- Marissa (AE): Share an estimated Dedicated capacity quote and a short TCO sketch for the 12-month commit.
- MediCore: Share a representative load trace (or sample traffic profile) and confirm primary region (us-east / us-west).

Could you confirm the decision criteria above and note any changes (e.g., tighter p95 target, higher concurrency)? Once we have that we’ll lock the MAP and Diego will run a tailored benchmark.

Attached: 20260502-demo-benchmarks.csv, redwood-performance-checklist.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to the next call.

—
Connor O'Brien
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Aria Gupta <aria.gupta@medicore.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam Carter <liam.carter@medicore.com>
Date: Fri, 2 May 2026 18:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo performance recap & decision checklist

Connor — thanks for the detailed recap and for running the numbers in real time. Helpful. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the CSV quickly:

1) p95 target: We need the hard p95 requirement to be <= 200ms for interactive clinical workflows (this is non-negotiable for launch). If you think that is achievable with a different config (dedicated capacity, quantized variant, lighter context), please outline the expected trade-offs.

2) Concurrency: Our production baseline will be closer to 300 concurrent active sessions during peak (not requests/min) with the ability to handle 600 concurrent short bursts during campaign spikes. We realize this is higher than the demo — that will change the topology.

3) Streaming: initial token within 80ms is what our clinicians notice as acceptable, subsequent tokens can be up to 60ms.

4) Private deployment: for PHI reasons we need to evaluate Private (VPC) deployment. Please include what additional latency we should expect on-prem / VPC vs hosted.

Next steps from us:
- I’ll send a 48-hour sample of anonymized traffic from our staging cluster (will redact PHI) and an outline of peak session patterns.
- We need a dedicated perf validation call with your SE + infra folks. Tue/Wed next week works for us as well.

Decision timeline: our engineering leadership wants go/no-go for the initial pilot by end of next week (May 9).

Thanks — Aria
Aria Gupta
Head of Platform Engineering, MediCore Health
aria.gupta@medicore.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Aria Gupta <aria.gupta@medicore.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 May 2026 19:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo performance recap & decision checklist

Aria — great notes, thank you. Quick replies inline and updated MAP below. We can absolutely be more aggressive in the tuning plan; it’s just a matter of configuration and validation.

- p95 <= 200ms: Achievable with a combination of dedicated capacity (consistent GPU pool), aggressive KV/cache warm policies, and moving to the 8-bit quantized runtime. Diego will show expected delta vs FP16 on the perf call.
- Concurrency 300 steady / 600 bursts: That moves this to a multi-host deployment. We’ll produce a sizing recommendation (hosts, GPU types, autoscale headroom).
- Streaming latency: we can aim for initial token < 80ms; Diego will validate single-token startup cost and pipeline priming techniques.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): expect an additional network hop which can add ~10–40ms depending on topology — we’ll include measured ranges.

Updated MAP (to be delivered by May 8 unless we agree otherwise):
1) Redwood deliverables: benchmark CSV (done), one-page trade-off doc (attached in Drive link), detailed MAP doc (mutual-action-plan-20260502.docx).
2) Technical validation: Diego + infra to run tailored benchmark against anonymized 48-hour sample trace from MediCore; target date for run: May 5.
3) Pricing/Capacity: Marissa to deliver Dedicated capacity estimate + 12-month TCO by May 6.
4) Decision: MediCore to deliver pilot go/no-go by May 9.

Can Diego and Marissa propose two time slots for the perf validation call? I’ll lock whichever works with MediCore.

—Connor

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 00:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo performance recap & decision checklist

Connor / Marissa / Evelyn — forwarding the thread so we can track the specific perf asks. Aria is tightening p95 to 200ms and needs 300–600 concurrent sessions. That changes the sizing plan; we’ll need:

- A representative sample of session start/stop timing (spike profile) and percent of streaming vs single-turn queries. Please ask MediCore to redact PHI and provide at least 48 hours of trace in CSV.
- Confirmation of desired primary region (Aria mentioned US; need us-east vs us-west).
- Any constraints on model variants (if they must use quantized only).

Proposed immediate actions:
1) I’ll draft a perf-run plan (tooling, warmup, KV-cache priming, load generator profile) and share by EOD Mon.
2) Connor, can you upload the demo CSV and the one-pager to the HubSpot deal record? I’ll reference it in the plan.

Notes: expect multi-host baseline for 300 steady concurrency on the 20B quantized model; I’ll estimate host counts after I see the trace.

—Diego
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
